 Journalists’ Pension Scheme: Arunachal Pradesh Cabinet To Consider Proposal On December 9
 Arunachal Pradesh CM Pema Khandu said the journalists’ pension scheme proposal will be placed before the state Cabinet on December 9, 2026
 Sanchi Varma Updated on: 16 November 2026 6:33 pm Updated on: 16 November 2026 6:33 pm SUBSCRIBE 
 Arunachal Pradesh Journalists’ Pension Scheme Photo: AI Arunachal Pradesh Journalists’ Pension Scheme Photo: AI Summary of this article
 Scheme was first announced in 2019.
 Cabinet to consider proposal on December 9.
 Pension amount and eligibility details remain unannounced.
 The Arunachal Pradesh government is preparing to take forward a long-pending pension scheme for working journalists under the leadership of Chief Minister Pema Khandu. The CM announced that the proposal will be placed before the state Cabinet at its next meeting on December 09, 2026. This move is expected to pave the way for the scheme’s implementation within December. This scheme would provide financial support to eligible journalists after retirement.

 Continue Reading Speaking to media persons on the occasion of National Press Day in Itanagar on November 16, 2026, Khandu acknowledged this delay in the implementation of this pension scheme, which was originally announced way back in 2019.
 According to PTI, he said that the government recognises the important role played by journalists in society and is committed to addressing their welfare concerns. He further revealed that the proposal has reached its final stage following discussions with the Arunachal Press Club (APC) and the concerned government department. He also referred to a meeting that was held with representatives of the Press Club on November 06, 2026; this led to his decision to take this matter up in the next Cabinet meeting.
 The Arunachal Pradesh Working Journalists’ Pension Scheme is a proposed welfare initiative aimed at providing financial security to journalists after they retire. The scheme was initially announced back in 2019, but it remained pending for years despite repeated discussions between the state government and representatives from the media. This initiative is expected to address the financial challenges faced by journalists who may not have access to structured retirement benefits or regular pension arrangements after leaving active service.
 However, details regarding this pension scheme are yet to be officially announced. Hence, journalists and beneficiaries of this scheme must wait for any official notice entailing details related to the monthly pension amount, eligibility conditions, minimum years of service, age requirements and applications. These details can be expected to be cleared following the Cabinet’s consideration of the proposal.
 Why has the decision been delayed?
 The pension scheme has been a long-standing demand of journalists’ organisations in Arunachal Pradesh. The Arunachal Press Club and the Arunachal Pradesh Union of Working Journalists (APUWJ) have repeatedly urged the government to expedite its implementation. The organisation raised concerns about delays and interventions from the state. The proposal had faced administrative hurdles despite discussions with the Department of Information and Public Relations.
 The December 09, 2026, meeting will be an important step towards determining the future of the pension scheme. If the proposal receives the necessary approval, the government could move towards formalising its implementation during the same month. The development could also strengthen the state’s broader effort to improve social security and working conditions for media professionals.
